artifacts_produced.deploy_evidence: READ-ONLY helper: load_context() (live S3 reads of the newest article_security_mention gold snapshot, every source's latest silver article rows, and a live universe_securities.build() alias table) + rederive_row/rederive_all, which call publication_gold._security_mentions and publication_gold.assign_tier on the STORED silver text -- never on the gold row's own stored mention_in_title/mention_in_lead/mention_count fields. No S3 write, no S3 delete, no vendor call anywhere in the module.

AC1's literal invocation. Prints the newest-snapshot denominator, the silver-text-available count, the AGREE/DISAGREE split over measurable rows, every disagreeing row (article_key, stored tier, derived tier, four text-derived inputs), the UNMEASURABLE bucket split by reason (never folded into a match or a mismatch), and which of the four inputs were recomputed from text (all four).

AC2's literal invocation. Prints the stored vs re-derived A/B/C/D tier distribution with denominator, a degeneracy flag for each, and all 16 rows of the (mention_in_title, mention_in_lead, mention_count>=2, share>=share_b) truth table with the tier each maps to, each combination run twice to show determinism, and a totality verdict.

AC3's literal invocation. Row grain: compares every mention row's stored signal_weight to WEIGHTS[stored signal_tier]. Day grain: compares every chatter_daily row's stored mention_score to the tier-weighted sum of that (security, day)'s own mention rows, denominator = chatter_daily rows checked, with one worked example (arithmetic shown) and every disagreeing pair named.

acceptance.criterion_verbatim: THE STORED TIER IS MATCHED AGAINST A RE-DERIVATION FROM THE STORED TEXT, with a printed denominator. Print: the number of gold article_security_mention rows examined out of the total in the newest snapshot; how many had their silver article text AVAILABLE (a row whose text cannot be read is UNMEASURABLE and is counted separately, never as a match or a mismatch); then AGREE / DISAGREE counts over the measurable rows, and EVERY disagreeing row named with its article_key, its stored signal_tier, the re-derived tier, and the four inputs that produced the re-derivation. A bare match rate with no disagreement list FAILS this criterion. State plainly which of the four inputs you recomputed from text and which you could not

acceptance.criterion_verbatim: AGREEMENT IS SEPARATED FROM A DEGENERATE DISTRIBUTION -- a 100% match on a corpus that is 100% one tier proves nothing. Print the tier distribution of the STORED grades and of the RE-DERIVED grades side by side (counts per A/B/C/D with the denominator), so a collapse to a single tier is visible. Then prove assign_tier's TOTALITY as its docstring claims: enumerate the (mention_in_title, mention_in_lead, mention_count>=2, share>=share_b) truth-table -- 16 combinations -- and show each maps to EXACTLY ONE tier with no combination unmapped and none mapping twice. Print all 16 rows

Full 16-row truth table printed (title=lead=count>=2=share>=share_b=True -> A weight 1.0; title=True,lead=False,count>=2=False,share>=share_b=False -> B weight 0.6; title=False,lead=False,count>=2=True,share>=share_b=False -> C weight 0.3; title=False,lead=False,count>=2=False,share>=share_b=False -> D weight 0.1; every one of the 16 rows deterministic_on_replay=true and tier_is_defined=true).
acceptance.denominator: measurable-rows denominator 263 of 263 for the distribution; 16 of 16 truth-table combinations printed and mapped to exactly one tier, 0 unmapped

acceptance.criterion_verbatim: THE STORED WEIGHT AND SCORE AGREE WITH THE STORED TIER. For every measurable row, show the weight assign_tier returns for the stored tier equals the weight the row carries (or state that the row carries no weight column, which is itself the finding); and at the DAY grain show that chatter_daily's mention_score equals the tier-weighted sum of its own day's rows, with the denominator of (security, day) pairs checked and every disagreeing pair named. If mention_score is not reproducible from the stored rows, say so with the arithmetic shown for one failing day -- that is FWD-4's answer either way, and a criterion that only reports "consistent" without showing one worked example FAILS
acceptance.denominator: 263 of 263 mention rows checked at row grain (0 missing signal_weight, 0 mismatches); 50997 of 50997 chatter_daily (security, day) pairs checked at day grain, 0 disagreeing pairs
